entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 42.7 +/- 10.9 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, V1162 Aql: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 42.7 +/- 10.9 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478). No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5625 +/- 168 K from Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 202, Name='V1162 Aql', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5625 +/- 168 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic).

entries.subject: Colour
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 5,625 K, because interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.205 +/- 0.021 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation, through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffefe5. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: skipped; gaia-xp: skipped; pulkovo: skipped; kiehling: skipped; kharitonov: skipped; burnashev: skipped; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,625 K and log g 0.4 (u1 0.556, u2 0.148): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

entries.subject: Surface gravity
entries.finding: Unmeasured, bounded: no gravity of this star is published (none in SIMBAD); Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra) gives the class's range, log g -1.33 to 2.86. Across log g 0 to 2.85, the part the grid covers, the limb laws differ by at most 1.9% of the centre brightness from the one drawn, at log g 0.4, the gravity closest to all of them; log g 0.4 is a display choice, not a measurement.

entries.subject: Light curve
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 vari_cepheid, source 4190143160245024256: 3 G-band harmonics of a 5.376177765929336 d period, peak-to-peak 0.430 mag; the harmonics reproduce the row's epoch of maximum and peak-to-peak amplitude. The page plays it as a veil over the disc from the scene date, phase known to 0.01 of a cycle there.
